entries.name: Holmwood Capital Advisors, LLC, and Holmwood Capital, LLC v. HC Government Realty Holdings, L.P., et al.

arguments_rejected_or_waived: Defendants' argument that the Termination Fee Estimate properly reduced Stockholders' Equity, and that reading "other non-cash items" in Adjustment One to include it would make Adjustment Two surplusage: rejected. The Estimate is a non-cash item that impacted GAAP stockholders' equity. Adjustment Two still has work to do for non-cash items GAAP would not permit HC REIT to record (e.g., internally generated goodwill, which Plaintiffs identified).

Defendants' argument that "builds" means "maintains," so the 3.0x multiplier is lost if Stockholders' Equity later falls below $35 million: rejected. "Builds" carries no temporal limitation, the parties imposed temporal limits elsewhere in the agreement (fn. 162), and the Court will not add omitted terms.

Defendants' argument that dividends were improperly added back to Stockholders' Equity: the Court agreed that "retained earnings" plainly excludes dividends, but held the argument waived. HC REIT knew of the deviation and delivered its final Termination Fee calculation on March 31, 2020 adding back dividends.

Defendants' argument that the Contributed Properties were overvalued by about $3.2 million: waived for the same reason. Alternatively rejected on the merits, assuming without deciding that the Court may second-guess the valuation. Scott's appraisal contained obvious errors, and its $2 million defeasance deduction would be a windfall because title later passed free and clear and no defeasance fee was paid.

Plaintiffs' argument that Section 10(f) lets HCA choose the form of Termination Fee Securities, and that Section 6(e)(ii) requires mutual consent before paying Acquisition Fees in common stock: rejected. Contra proferentem was applied against the Founder-drafted instrument, and Stanton's self-interested testimony was the only extrinsic evidence.

Plaintiffs' argument that Side Letter § 1 requires HCA to repay only reimbursements it actually received: rejected. The ambiguity was construed against Plaintiffs, so HCA must pay all O&O Expenses above the 15% cap.

Plaintiffs' argument that Holmwood could not have breached the Contribution Agreement because it had no obligation to procure lien releases before closing: rejected as conflating obligations. The separate No-Default Representation proved false.

Plaintiffs' argument that Contribution Agreement § 6.A allocates consent costs to Holdings, so Defendants suffered no damages: rejected. Section 6.A applies only to consents Holmwood procured before closing, and Holmwood procured none.

Plaintiffs' argument that HCA is owed Acquisition Fees for the Disputed Acquisitions because Defendants prevented performance through the Amended Investment Guidelines: rejected. Nothing prevented HCA from proposing acquisitions to the Board.

Plaintiffs' argument that the Shortfall Amounts were loans payable on demand at 8% interest (12% per internal Holmwood documents): not proven. Only Stanton's self-serving testimony supported the existence of a loan agreement.

authorities_cited.authority: Management Agreement § 1(a) (definitions of "Stockholders' Equity," "Asset Management Fee" and "Termination Fee")
authorities_cited.proposition: Stockholders' Equity excludes "other non-cash items ... that have impacted stockholders' equity" as reported under GAAP (Adjustment One) and includes "retained earnings"; the Termination Fee is 3x fees earned over the 24-month look-back plus accrued, unpaid Acquisition Fees.

authorities_cited.authority: Side Letter § 3
authorities_cited.proposition: Sets the Termination Fee multiplier by whether HC REIT "builds" Stockholders' Equity of $15 million or $35 million; construed as a high-water mark.

authorities_cited.authority: Management Agreement §§ 10(f), 6(e)(ii)
authorities_cited.proposition: Ambiguous provisions on who selects Termination Fee Securities and Acquisition Fee Securities, construed to permit HC REIT to pay in common stock without HCA's input.

authorities_cited.authority: Side Letter § 1
authorities_cited.proposition: Ambiguous O&O repayment provision, construed to require HCA to pay all O&O Expenses above 15% of gross Offering proceeds.

authorities_cited.authority: Contribution Agreement § 11.C (No-Default Representation)
authorities_cited.proposition: Holmwood represented that entering into the agreement would not cause a default under any mortgage or contract; breached by the unconsented transfer of the CMBS profits interest.

authorities_cited.authority: Contribution Agreement § 6.A
authorities_cited.proposition: Holdings bears the cost only of consents Holmwood procures before closing; inapplicable where no consent was procured.

authorities_cited.authority: CMBS Loan Agreement § 4.2.1
authorities_cited.proposition: Requires the lender's prior written consent to transfer any interest in the CMBS Properties, including assignment of profits.

authorities_cited.authority: Stockman v. Heartland Indus. P'rs, L.P., 2009 WL 2096213 (Del. Ch. July 14, 2009)
authorities_cited.proposition: Contra proferentem applies to ambiguous terms in instruments making promises to non-negotiating investors; the drafter bears the onus of clarity.

authorities_cited.authority: Murfey v. WHC Ventures, LLC, 236 A.3d 337 (Del. 2020)
authorities_cited.proposition: Courts cannot rewrite contracts or supply omitted provisions; applied to reject reading "builds" as "maintains."

authorities_cited.proposition: The elements of waiver: a requirement exists, the waiving party knew of it, and it intended to waive.

authorities_cited.proposition: Applies the dictionary meaning of "paid" ("marked by the receipt of pay") to an unambiguous contract.

authorities_cited.proposition: Breach of contract requires proof of a contract, breach and damages; Plaintiffs failed to prove a loan contract existed.

authorities_cited.proposition: Claimants and counterclaimants must prove each element by a preponderance of the evidence.

summary.brief_summary: After a three-day trial, Vice Chancellor David resolved claims by HCA and Holmwood against HC REIT and Holdings over the Termination Fee and related fees, together with counterclaims for breach of the Management and Contribution Agreements and unjust enrichment. The Court held that the accrued Termination Fee Estimate must be added back to Stockholders' Equity, that the Side Letter's "builds" test is a high-water mark, and that HC REIT waived its belated dividend and overvaluation adjustments by delivering its final fee calculation without them. Applying contra proferentem because the Founders drafted the instruments for a vehicle they intended to market to investors, the Court construed the ambiguous payment-form and O&O provisions against Plaintiffs. It also held Holmwood liable for $517,463.35 for breaching its no-default representation by transferring the CMBS profits interest without lender consent.
summary.core_legal_issue: Following trial on cross-claims arising from HC REIT's non-renewal of HCA's Management Agreement, the principal questions were: (1) whether an accrued GAAP liability for the estimated Termination Fee had to be added back to "Stockholders' Equity" as an "other non-cash item[]"; (2) whether the Side Letter's requirement that HC REIT "build" $35 million of Stockholders' Equity sets a high-water mark or a test at termination; and (3) related disputes over the form of fee securities, O&O Expense repayment, undocumented "loans," and Holmwood's breach of a no-default representation by contributing the CMBS Properties' profits interest without lender consent.
summary.disposition: judgment in part for each side
summary.holding: Mixed judgment after trial. Termination Fee (Complaint Count I): the Termination Fee Estimate is an "other non-cash item[]" under Adjustment One and must be added back to Stockholders' Equity. Defendants waived their dividend and Contributed Properties challenges by delivering the March 31, 2020 calculation without them, and the overvaluation claim also fails on the merits (assuming without deciding the Court may revisit the valuation). "Builds" means achieves, so the 3.0x multiplier applies "[i]f Stockholders' Equity equaled or exceeded $35 million at any time prior to the Termination Date." Asset Management Fees must be recalculated on that basis and include the 24-month period ending March 31, 2020 (fn. 165). Plaintiffs did not prove that accrued Acquisition Fees went unpaid, because recording the shares with the transfer agent was not shown to fall short of payment. HCA earned no Acquisition Fees for the Disputed Acquisitions because it rendered no services and was not prevented from performing. Fn. 117 notes an analogous "AMF Accrual Estimate" add-back that neither party briefed. Form of payment: applying contra proferentem against the Founder-drafted Management Agreement, HC REIT could pay both the Termination Fee and the Acquisition Fees in common stock. Shortfall Amounts (Complaint Count III): no loan contract was proven, but the parties intended repayment; they must meet and confer on a repayment proposal. O&O Expenses: HCA must bear all O&O Expenses above the 15% cap ($723,932 excess). The record does not show whether HCA paid less than that amount, so the parties must meet and confer and, if necessary, submit payment documentation; that answer determines whether HC REIT's dividend and distribution offset was proper (fn. 206). Counterclaim Count I (duplicative property management fees and $7,500 in undocumented reimbursements): not proven; judgment for HCA. Counterclaim Count II: Holmwood breached the No-Default Representation; Defendants recover $517,463.35. The Bring-Down Representations breach yielded no proven additional damages. Counterclaim Count III (unjust enrichment): judgment for Plaintiffs. The parties must meet and confer in good faith to prepare a revised Termination Fee calculation jointly, and to submit a proposed form of order implementing the rulings.
key_facts_and_concessions: When CFO Piscetelli calculated Q3 2019 Asset Management Fees, she began treating the $1,750,000 Termination Fee Estimate (accrued under GAAP and reported in the Form 1-SA) as a liability. This cut Q2 2019 Stockholders' Equity from $37,133,134 to $34,904,007, below the Side Letter's $35 million threshold. HC REIT's March 31, 2020 Termination Fee of $1,645,453 used a 1.5x multiplier.
The parties agree the Termination Fee Estimate does not fall within Adjustment Two, which requires Board approval (fn. 126).

On July 12, 2019, Post (HCA's then-CFO) told Piscetelli that "dividends and distributions" were "excluded from common stock." Piscetelli said she might "adjust, if necessary" but never did. HC REIT's final March 31, 2020 Termination Fee calculation added back dividends, and HC REIT first raised the issue in a June 18, 2025 expert report.
Plaintiffs do not argue that adding back dividends was proper under the Management Agreement (fn. 149).

The Founders controlled HCA, HC REIT and Holdings when the Management Agreement was signed and expected HC REIT to be marketed to outside investors. HC REIT issued a preliminary offering circular within months.

Holmwood did not obtain consent from the CMBS lender before the Exchange Transaction. LNR, the servicer, issued a notice of default on November 16, 2022, and HC REIT spent $517,463.35 obtaining a Consent and Loan Modification Agreement on March 27, 2023.
At deposition, Stanton conceded that HCA "did not provide those services" for the three Disputed Acquisitions (fn. 177).

Holmwood transferred $408,514 in Shortfall Amounts to HC REIT without signed contracts. HC REIT does not deny receipt, its Form 1-K acknowledged the payable, and the parties agree the amounts were not a gift.
summary.practical_takeaway: A party that delivers a final contractual fee calculation after being told how its inputs deviate from the contract risks waiving later challenges to those inputs, so objections should be raised before the calculation is tendered. Founder-affiliated managers of vehicles intended for outside investors should draft fee-mechanics provisions unambiguously, because the Court will construe ambiguities against them even when the same founders sat on both sides.
summary.standard_of_review: Post-trial; each claimant and counterclaimant had to prove every element, including damages, by a preponderance of the evidence. Contracts were read under Delaware's objective theory and plain meaning. Ambiguous provisions (held ambiguous on summary judgment) were construed by contra proferentem rather than by extrinsic evidence.
